Packing for a 2-Day Motorcycle Trip

A two-day motorcycle overnighter is the perfect introduction to touring. Short enough that mistakes aren't catastrophic, long enough to feel like a proper adventure. The key is packing smart — bring what you need, leave what you don't. Here's your complete guide.

The Golden Rule: Pack Light

For a single overnight, you need far less than you think. A tail bag or small tank bag is often enough. Resist the urge to fill panniers to the brim — extra weight affects handling, fuel economy, and your enjoyment of the ride.

Clothing (Off-Bike)

  • One change of casual clothes (jeans/trousers, t-shirt, lightweight jumper)
  • Underwear and socks for day two
  • Lightweight packable shoes or trainers for evenings
  • Swimwear if your accommodation has a hot tub or you fancy a wild swim

Riding Gear

  • Your regular riding kit worn on the bike
  • Waterproof over-layer: Even if the forecast is clear, pack waterproofs. UK weather lies.
  • Spare gloves in a zip-lock bag (wet gloves on day two is miserable)
  • Neck tube for cold morning starts
  • Clear visor insert or spare visor for night/fog riding

Tech and Navigation

  • Phone with offline maps downloaded for your route area
  • USB charging cable and plug adapter
  • Power bank (at least 10,000mAh)
  • Camera or action cam if you want to capture the ride
  • Headphones for evening (small, lightweight)

Tools and Emergency Kit

You don't need a full workshop, but a few essentials can save the weekend:

  • Tyre repair kit and CO2 inflators (or a mini compressor)
  • Multi-tool or basic spanner set for your bike
  • Cable ties and electrical tape
  • Chain lube (small can)
  • First aid kit (compact)
  • Torch or head torch

Toiletries (Miniature)

  • Travel toothbrush and toothpaste
  • Deodorant
  • Any medication you take
  • Sunscreen (small tube)
  • Lip balm with SPF
Pro tip: Decant everything into travel-size containers. Hotel toiletries handle the rest. If you're camping, add a microfibre towel — they pack tiny and dry fast.

Documents and Money

  • Driving licence
  • Bank card and small amount of cash (some rural places are card-only or cash-only — be prepared for both)
  • Accommodation booking confirmation
  • Breakdown cover details

Packing Strategy

Roll clothing instead of folding — it saves space and reduces creasing. Use dry bags or zip-lock bags to separate clean clothes from dirty and keep everything waterproof. Even "waterproof" luggage can let water in at seams during a sustained downpour.

Load heavy items low and close to the bike's centre of gravity. A top-heavy tail bag will make the bike feel unstable through corners. If using a tank bag, don't overload it to the point where it blocks your view of the instruments.

What NOT to Pack

Leave these at home:

  • A laptop (you're on a motorcycle tour, not a business trip)
  • More than two days of clothing
  • Full-size toiletries
  • Anything you'd be devastated to lose or damage

Two days, one overnight, minimal kit. That's the recipe for a stress-free motorcycle weekend. Now stop reading lists and go ride.

Pack waterproofs even on a clear forecast, plus spare gloves in a zip-lock bag.
Roll clothing rather than folding it, and use dry bags to keep everything waterproof.
Carry a bank card and some cash, as rural places can be card-only or cash-only.
Leave the laptop, full-size toiletries and anything you would hate to lose or damage at home.

faq.q: How much luggage do I need for one overnight?
faq.a: Far less than you think. A tail bag or small tank bag is often enough for a single overnight. Resist filling panniers to the brim, because extra weight affects handling, fuel economy and your enjoyment of the ride. Pack one change of casual clothes, spare underwear and socks, and your riding kit worn on the bike.

faq.q: Do I really need waterproofs if the forecast is clear?
faq.a: Yes. UK weather lies, and a clear forecast can turn into a downpour within an hour. Pack a waterproof over-layer even on a dry day, and keep spare gloves in a zip-lock bag so day two does not begin with cold, wet hands, which destroy concentration.

faq.q: What is the best way to pack clothes on a bike?
faq.a: Roll clothing instead of folding it, which saves space and reduces creasing. Use dry bags or zip-lock bags to separate clean from dirty and keep everything waterproof, because even luggage sold as waterproof can leak at the seams during a sustained downpour. Load heavy items low and central for stable handling.

faq.q: Should I carry cash on a weekend trip?
faq.a: Yes. Bring a bank card and a small amount of cash, because some rural pubs, campsites and fuel stations are card-only while others are cash-only. Being prepared for both means you are never caught out at the one place between you and a bed for the night.

faq.q: What should I leave at home?
faq.a: Leave the laptop, more than two days of clothing, full-size toiletries and anything you would be devastated to lose or damage. Decant toiletries into travel-size containers and let hotel supplies handle the rest. If you are camping, add a microfibre towel, which packs tiny and dries fast.
